description: Is the rise in mean Life expectancy over 2000 to 2015 the same for Developing and Developed countries, or does the gap between them narrow?
code:
# %%
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from agent.execution.runtime import (
    df,
    load,
    publish,
    record_fact,
    record_model,
    save_chart,
)

# %%
LE_COL=[c for c in df.columns if c.strip()=="Life expectancy"][0]
d=df[["Year","Status",LE_COL]].copy()
d.columns=["Year","Status","LE"]
d["Status"]=d["Status"].astype(str).str.strip()
d["Year"]=d["Year"].astype(int)
d=d[(d.Year>=2000)&(d.Year<=2015)]
def q1(s): return s.quantile(0.25)
def q3(s): return s.quantile(0.75)
aggf=dict(count="count",mean="mean",median="median",sd="std",q1=q1,q3=q3)
gs=d.groupby(["Year","Status"])["LE"].agg(**aggf).round(3)
print(gs.unstack("Status").to_string())
ys=d.groupby("Year")["LE"].agg(**aggf).round(3)
print(ys.to_string())
gap=(gs.xs("Developed",level="Status")["mean"]-gs.xs("Developing",level="Status")["mean"]).round(3)
print(gap.to_string())
tbl={}
for (y,s),r in gs.iterrows():
    tbl[f"{y}_{s}"]={k:float(v) for k,v in r.items()}
record_fact("eda4_le_year_status_stats",tbl,"Count, mean, median, SD, Q1, Q3 of Life expectancy by Year and Status, 2000-2015, years")
yt={str(y):{k:float(v) for k,v in r.items()} for y,r in ys.iterrows()}
record_fact("eda4_le_year_stats",yt,"Count, mean, median, SD, Q1, Q3 of Life expectancy by Year, all Status, 2000-2015, years")
record_fact("eda4_gap_by_year",{str(y):float(v) for y,v in gap.items()},"Developed minus Developing mean Life expectancy by Year, years")

# %%
dev=gs.xs('Developed',level='Status')
dng=gs.xs('Developing',level='Status')
rise_dev=float(dev.loc[2015,'mean']-dev.loc[2000,'mean'])
rise_dng=float(dng.loc[2015,'mean']-dng.loc[2000,'mean'])
g0=float(gap.loc[2000]); g1=float(gap.loc[2015])
record_fact('eda4_rise_by_status',{'developed_mean_rise':round(rise_dev,3),'developing_mean_rise':round(rise_dng,3),'gap_2000':g0,'gap_2015':g1,'gap_change':round(g1-g0,3)},'Change in mean Life expectancy 2000 to 2015 by Status and change in Developed-Developing mean gap, years')
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8,4.5))
ax.plot(dev.index,dev['mean'],marker='o',label='Developed')
ax.plot(dng.index,dng['mean'],marker='o',label='Developing')
ax.set_title('Mean Life expectancy by Year and Status, 2000-2015')
ax.set_xlabel('Year')
ax.set_ylabel('Mean Life expectancy (years)')
ax.legend()
ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
save_chart(fig,'eda4_mean_le_by_status','Mean Life expectancy by Year for Developed and Developing countries, 2000-2015 (years)')
print(round(rise_dev,3),round(rise_dng,3),g0,g1)

# %%
mm=(ys['mean']-ys['median']).round(3)
print(mm.to_string())
record_fact('eda4_mean_median_gap_by_year',{str(y):float(v) for y,v in mm.items()},'Mean minus median Life expectancy by Year, all Status, 2000-2015, years')
cnt=gs['count'].unstack('Status')
print(cnt.iloc[[0,-1]].to_string())
record_fact('eda4_rows_by_year_status',{str(y):{s:float(cnt.loc[y,s]) for s in cnt.columns} for y in cnt.index},'Row counts by Year and Status, 2000-2015')

findings.statement: Mean Life expectancy rose more for Developing countries than for Developed countries from 2000 to 2015: Developing rose 5.07 years (64.62 to 69.69) and Developed rose 3.91 years (76.80 to 80.71). Row counts are 32 Developed and 151 Developing in every Year, 183 in total per Year.

The Developed-Developing gap in mean Life expectancy narrowed from 12.18 years in 2000 to 11.02 years in 2015, a change of -1.16 years. The gap was not monotonic: it widened to 13.01 in 2004, dipped to 11.52 in 2008, and was 11.02 in 2015.

Across all Status groups, the mean minus median Life expectancy gap moved from -4.25 years in 2000 to -2.28 years in 2015, so the mean sits closer to the median by 2015. This is the only spread-related claim supported by the recorded facts.

Mean and median Life expectancy by Year and Status for 2000 to 2015, with counts, are in the recorded table. Developed 2000 mean 76.80 and median 77.7; Developing 2000 mean 64.62 and median 67.4; Developed 2015 mean 80.71; Developing 2015 mean 69.69. Overall, the Year means rose from 66.75 in 2000 to 71.62 in 2015.

follow_ups: What drives the faster rise in Developing Life expectancy, for example Adult Mortality, HIV/AIDS, schooling or income composition?
Why did the Developed-Developing gap peak in 2004 and fall to 11.5 years by 2008?
Are per-Year SD and Q1/Q3 changing for each Status group, which would be needed before any claim about spread?

brief.question: Is the rise in mean Life expectancy over 2000 to 2015 the same for Developing and Developed countries, or does the gap between them narrow?
brief.complete_when: Reports mean and median Life expectancy by Year 2000 to 2015 for each Status group, with row counts per group and year, and states whether the Developed-Developing gap widens, narrows or stays flat.

reviews.reasoning: Checked the headline numbers against the cited facts. Developing rise 64.62 to 69.69 = 5.07 and Developed rise 76.80 to 80.71 = 3.91 match eda4_rise_by_status and eda4_le_year_status_stats. Row counts of 32 Developed and 151 Developing per Year match eda4_rows_by_year_status. The gap of 12.18 in 2000 and 11.02 in 2015 (change -1.16) matches eda4_gap_by_year and eda4_rise_by_status. The non-monotone path (13.01 in 2004, 11.52 in 2008) matches eda4_gap_by_year. The 2000 medians (77.7 and 67.4) match the status stats, and the Year means 66.75 to 71.62 match eda_1. The mean-minus-median movement from -4.25 to about -2.3 is consistent with eda4_mean_median_gap_by_year and the accepted eda_1 finding. The code computes these as stated, and the automatic checks report no problems. The brief is answered: it gives the gap direction (narrows, not monotone) and the per-group, per-year statistics are recorded as facts. The report is appropriately descriptive and makes no inferential claim it cannot support. Accepting.
